reportedHostedInterpreter: CPython 3.15.2 (recorded executable path; its installed stdlib bytes were not retained)
upstreamObservation: The macOS kqueue wait catches OSError and falls back; InterruptedError subclasses OSError. A handler raising InterruptedError while control is waiting can therefore lose the first stop request inside that catch.
inference: Consistent with first TERM being swallowed during the timed kqueue wait, followed by the parent 12-second timeout. The fallback signals owned processes and immediately kills the helper without a second grace period; this can prevent its final receipt. This is not proof of the exact suspended frame or the original consent failure cause.
receiptLimitation: Later collect/cleanup calls overwrite capture-cleanup.json, so the retained final identityMatched=false values cannot reconstruct the earlier escalation.
followUpOnly: Use a private stop exception outside the OSError hierarchy, or an explicit owned-child shutdown protocol.
